Triage: `pm:queue` + `domain:ui`, type Bug — the hook's own docstring declares stability protection for exactly the no-provider case where it measurably lapses (declared ≠ enforced, with a measured downstream consequence in `ObjectDataTable.derivedColumns`). The option-1 vs option-2 choice (bind the frozen fallback vs stabilize the memo key) is the implementer's, **with one dispatch clause**: whichever is chosen must pin the late-instance transition (a provider appearing after first render) so the two options' behavioural difference the card flags is a test, not a surprise. Assert on identity/recompute counts, not on rendered output — the card's own guidance.

**Claim:** `domain:ui` execution seat, session `session_012u2pRjcqAYtoEjgr3wwhnK` · branch `claude/issue-5564-safe-field-label-identity` · round 4.

## ⛔ Option 1 is not the "smallest change" the card says it is — measured

The card offers two options and calls option 1 (return `SAFE_FIELD_LABEL_FALLBACK` when there is no instance) the smallest, "already the intended shape". I measured that on `origin/main` before dispatching, and **as literally written it is a breaking runtime change**:

- `useObjectLabel()`'s memo returns an object with **27 members**: `objectLabel`, `objectDescription`, `fieldLabel`, `fieldOptionLabel`, `translateOptions`, `appLabel`, `appDescription`, `navGroupLabel`, `dashboardLabel`, `dashboardDescription`, `dashboardActionLabel`, `widgetTitle`, `widgetDescription`, `widgetSubCaption`, `pageLabel`, `reportLabel`, `viewLabel`, `viewDescription`, `viewEmptyState`, `sectionLabel`, `actionLabel`, `actionConfirm`, `actionSuccess`, `actionDescription`, `actionResultDialog`, `actionParamText`, `actionParamOptionLabel`.
- `SAFE_FIELD_LABEL_FALLBACK` has **5**: `fieldLabel`, `translateOptions`, `fieldOptionLabel`, `sectionLabel`, `actionLabel`.

So option 1 drops 22 members on the no-provider path — the exact path the wrapper advertises. Most callers destructure only within the five, but **three take the whole object**, and one of them calls outside the set:

```
packages/plugin-detail/src/renderers/record-reference-rail.tsx:109   const i18n = useSafeFieldLabel() as any;   →  i18n.objectLabel(...)
packages/plugin-detail/src/renderers/record-related-list.tsx:88      const i18n = useSafeFieldLabel();
packages/plugin-tree/src/ObjectTree.tsx:368                          const i18n = useSafeFieldLabel();  →  i18n.fieldLabel(...)
```

`record:reference-rail` would get `i18n.objectLabel is not a function` outside a provider. `useSafeFieldLabel` is also publicly exported (`packages/i18n/src/index.ts:60`), so external consumers can reach any of the 27.

**This does not veto option 1** — it means option 1 costs completing the fallback to all 27 members, which changes its size argument. Weigh it against option 2 (stabilize the memo key on something that does not churn without an instance) with that cost included, and **state which you chose and why**. If you pick option 1, the fallback must cover every member the real object exposes, and a test must pin that the two shapes agree — otherwise the next member added to `useObjectLabel` silently reintroduces the crash.

## Triage's dispatch clause is binding

Whichever option you choose **must pin the late-instance transition** — a provider appearing after first render — so the behavioural difference between the two options is a test rather than a surprise. Assert on identity / recompute counts, not on rendered output: nothing renders wrong today, so a rendering assertion is green against the broken code.

## Corroboration worth reading

`packages/plugin-charts/src/ObjectChart.tsx:268-271` already carries a hand-rolled ref workaround with this comment: *"the i18n hook returns a fresh function reference on every render, which would otherwise invalidate fetchData's useCallback identity and trigger an infinite refetch loop."* An independent consumer hit this and worked around it locally — useful evidence for the fix, and worth noting whether your change makes that workaround removable (do **not** remove it here; it is outside this surface).

Note also that the existing comment at `useSafeFieldLabel` asserts *"It already returns a stable memoized object"* — that is the declaration this card measures as false without an instance. Correct it in the same stroke.

## Surface

`packages/i18n/src/useObjectLabel.ts` + tests + changeset. `packages/i18n` is a published package: no new exports, no signature changes beyond what the chosen option requires.

## ACCEPT — PR #5585

Gates read **by name** on head `b492c9796`, all 22 runs accounted for: `Test (shard 1/4)` `(2/4)` `(3/4)` `(4/4)`, `Type Check`, `Lint`, `Build & E2E`, `Build Docs`, `Bundle Analysis`, `Doc Snippet Type Check`, `Doc Component Type Check`, `Internal Docs Link Check`, `Changeset Declaration`, `Changeset Bump Policy`, `Changeset Fixed Group Check`, `Control Byte Scan`, `Skill Guide Path Check`, `Live E2E (informational)`, `label` — every one `completed: success`, plus the three usual `skipped` matrix no-ops. Console budget PASS; `useObjectLabel.js` 30.51 → 33.40 KB raw (7.57 → 8.71 gzipped), which is the predicate, two constants and their doc comments.

### Option 2 was the right call, and you found a better reason for it than I gave you

My dispatch framed the choice around what option 1 would **cost** — the 27-vs-5 shape gap and the `record-reference-rail` crash. You found that option 1 would not **work**, which is the stronger objection and the one that actually decides it:

> `ListView.filterFields` — the consumer `useObjectLabel`'s memo docstring names as its reason to exist — reaches the hook through `useListFieldLabel`, which calls `useObjectLabel()` **directly**.

Verified independently on `origin/main`:

```
packages/plugin-list/src/ListView.tsx:683   const { fieldLabel, actionLabel, objectLabel } = useObjectLabel();
packages/plugin-list/src/ListView.tsx:729   const { translateOptions } = useSafeFieldLabel();
```

The same file uses both hooks for different things, and the **filter fields** path — the named victim — is on the direct one. Option 1 touches only the wrapper, so it would have left the docstring's own example consumer broken.

Your "20+ other direct call sites" is also an under-claim: measured **33** direct `useObjectLabel()` call sites across 9 packages (`app-shell`, `components`, `core`, `layout`, `plugin-dashboard`, `plugin-form`, `plugin-list`, `plugin-timeline`, `react`), plus `ObjectTimeline.tsx:36-37`'s hand-rolled `useObjectLabel() ?? OBJECT_LABEL_FALLBACK`, confirmed.

### The correctness argument holds — I checked it rather than accepting it

The whole fix rests on the substitution being **unobservable**: that while the stand-ins are pinned, nothing can read them. Verified by enumerating every site in the module:

| site | gated by |
|---|---|
| `t(...)` at `:165` | inside `for (const ns of namespaces)`, `namespaces = getAppNamespaces()` at `:158` |
| `t(...)` at `:604` | inside `for (const ns of getAppNamespaces())` at `:602` |
| `i18n.language` `:131`, `i18n.getResourceBundle` `:132` | after `if (!hasUsableI18nInstance(i18n)) return []` at `:130` |

Those are the only `t()` calls and the only `i18n` reads in the file. So while unbound, `getAppNamespaces()` returns `[]`, both loops have zero iterations, and neither stand-in is reachable.

**Routing the memo key and the gate through one shared `hasUsableI18nInstance` is what makes that argument stable rather than merely true today.** Two separate predicates could have drifted into a window where the substitution is active but `getAppNamespaces()` returns a non-empty list — and then `NO_INSTANCE_T` would really be called. Collapsing the inline check at `:131` into the shared predicate closes that. Keeping `NO_INSTANCE_T` faithful to react-i18next's not-ready `t` is the correct belt-and-braces for the same reason.

### The card was wrong on one detail and you corrected it

The card attributes the churn to a fresh `t`/`i18n` **pair**. Only `i18n` churns — `t` is react-i18next's module-level `notReadyT`. Pinning both dependencies anyway is right: `t`'s stability is an implementation detail of a third-party package, not a contract.

### Tests

Five cases, all on identity/recompute counts. Two things raise this above the bar:

- **The global-instance detachment is asserted, not assumed.** `createI18n` registers itself globally via `initReactI18next`, so a probe meant to run unbound would otherwise silently bind to an earlier test's instance and assert nothing. Asserting the precondition is what stops the whole suite being vacuous.
- **Case 4 keeps the provider element at the same tree position** so the probe is *updated* rather than remounted when the instance arrives. A remount would reset the memo and prove nothing — that is exactly how a late-instance test passes for the wrong reason, and it was avoided deliberately.

Case 5 pins the 27-member surface on both paths and that `objectLabel` is callable unbound, which guards the `record-reference-rail` hazard permanently rather than relying on this PR's choice not to narrow it.

Ablation is a real ablation: 3 red / 2 green, and **the two that stayed green are the right two** (the with-instance guard and the shape pin).

### Follow-on

**#5587** filed — `ObjectChart`'s `fieldOptionLabel` ref workaround becomes removable once this lands, and `ObjectTimeline`'s `useSafeObjectLabel` is a third hand-rolled duplicate. Correctly not removed here: unwinding a refetch-loop guard wants its own review and its own test, not a ride-along in a diff about memo identity. I added the missing `finding` label so triage's queue can see it.

Proceeding to ready-for-review and the merge queue.
